prompt.text: Start in workspace.ipynb for Recover the sensor readings. This activity works for 1 to 4 people. Your personal Paper tutor link appears in your own JupyterLab view after chat connects. Open it on this laptop, then scan its QR code with your phone. You can use continuous capture or take/choose one photo at a time. Use this group chat for paper done, coding done, and submitted.

Phase 1: you have up to 20 minutes to design the sensor recovery on paper. Each recorded value includes one third of the previous true value; the value before the sequence is zero. Use the notebook example to derive a reusable representation for the whole recovery. Use your camera and private tutor for feedback. Type exactly paper done here when ready; in a group, each member types it. Use paper not done to withdraw readiness. Start coding only when I announce Phase 2.

Phase 2 starts now: you have up to 25 minutes. Stop camera capture and implement recover_readings(recorded) using the representation you derived on paper. There is one function and one check. In a group, take turns editing the shared notebook, one person at a time. Save before checking and keep the supplied cell tags. When the check passes and you understand the recovery, type exactly coding done here. Every member must type it; alone, your own message is sufficient. Use coding not done to withdraw readiness.

The coding phase has ended, either because everyone present was ready and the recovery check passed, or because the 25 minutes elapsed. Save your current work, including any unfinished code. Alone, run the final submission cell with your activity email; in a group, choose one person to submit for everyone. Wait for a submission ID, then type submitted here. The ID confirms storage. Keep it; your instructor can see the final score out of 1.
Thanks for confirming submission. Keep your submission ID and paper notes. Your instructor can see your stored notebook and final grade. This concludes the activity.
